items.description: South Cornwall coast from Lizard Point to Gribbin Head excluding the Tidal Fal Estuary
items.eaAreaName: Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
items.message:
High tides and forecast weather conditions over the next two days may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible up to 1 hour either side of high tide on Friday morning and Saturday morning. 
High water levels with some wave and spray overtopping may cause flooding to quaysides, harbours, and low lying land, roads and car parks.

High tide at Falmouth on Friday is at 06:36AM, with a forecast tide level of 2.4mAOD, which is around 0.1m above tide table levels.  Times and heights of high tide will vary along the coast. Force 5 Southerly winds and offshore waves of around 2m are forecast over high tide.

Coastal conditions should ease for Friday evening's high tide, however similar conditions are forecast over Saturday mornings high tide bringing a further risk of flooding. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 1:00PM on Friday 27 November or as the situation changes.

High tides, strong winds and large waves tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 07:15am to 09:15am on Friday 27th November. 
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers or on the coast, with spray being seen on the seafront paths. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. Please take notice of the Flood Sign at the top of South Beach Road. 
The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Kings Lynn of 3.2mAODN at 08:15am, on Friday 27th November, Wind Force 6, South-Easterly. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Friday 27 November or as the situation changes.

items.description: North Sea coast at Withernsea, Easington and Kilnsea
items.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding, though standing water and debris may still remain.
The previous tide of concern has now passed,  the weather is more settled and no flooding is expected.  
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.  
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.
